history.p: In December 1875 Gade wrote to Richard Peyton of the Birmingham Musical Festival that he had composed "Zion" expressly for the festival in 1876. However, the score is end-dated 16 September 1874, that is before he received the invitation from Birmingham. It just had not yet been performed. "Zion" is the second part of the trilogy of which "Kalanus" (NWGW 174) is the first and "The Crusaders" (NWGW 172) the third part.

physDesc.physMedium: Written in ink. Paper: 20 staves. Last two pages unnumbered. On the unnumbered verso of title page 23 bars in full score. From first music page paginated 1-28. With several cancellations and emendations. At the end of the music on p. 28 Gade has written: "Fine. Christiansborg den 29 October 1873."

Bound in cardboard cover with marbled sides and cloth spine. In the middle of the front cover a handwritten label inscribed "Zion" in Gade's hand and "Op. 49" added later in pencil in a foreign hand. Written in ink. Paginated 1-96. (19-20 bis and 42 a and B added). Verso of title page paginated 1a containing the introduction; the original p. 1 changed to p. b and all indications of instruments as well as the heading "I" above the music have been cancelled. At the end of the music on p. 96 Gade has written: "S.D.G. / [Gade's musical signature] / 16 September 1874 / Christiansborg".
